parallel.requirements: The run recognized the need for a pure Node.js ESM .mjs port in /output, exact manual argparse-compatible CLI behavior, Money amount halving, Decimal-style formatting, local-only imports, and black-box probing of the executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Although swarm mode was active, the main agent stated the migration was small and that a swarm would add overhead, so it kept ownership and used only a background shell process for the currency-code scan.
parallel.implementation: The main agent probed numeric, formatting, currency, and argparse behavior, then wrote pyfloat.mjs, decimal.mjs, money.mjs, argparse.mjs, currencies.mjs, and test6.mjs itself.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The main agent generated the currency registry from the completed scan result, wired local imports into test6.mjs, and delivered all expected .mjs files under /output.
parallel.verification: It checked the four samples, 50 edge cases, 250 fuzz cases, stderr/help comparisons, and a currency acceptance sweep before finalizing; official evaluation passed 120/120.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task work is visible at closure, and the official evaluator found no failing sample among the 120 tests.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same Node.js ESM, .mjs, manual CLI, no dependency, local module, no Python embedding, no Intl.NumberFormat/BigInt, and black-box behavior requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single main agent owned probing, implementation, module wiring, verification, and final response without delegation or child-agent activity.
serial.implementation: It probed executable behavior, wrote pyfloat.mjs, pydecimal.mjs, pystr.mjs, currencies.mjs, money.mjs, argparse.mjs, and test6.mjs, and modeled decimal/string/currency/argparse behavior locally.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial agent assembled the final entry file with local module imports and produced the expected test6.mjs plus supporting .mjs libraries in /output.
serial.verification: It ran the sample cases, a broad differential script, stderr/help checks, and random fuzz tests; official evaluation passed 120/120.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The differential script reported two expected help-program-name mismatches during a nonofficial check, but the agent explained them and the official evaluator passed all 120 tests.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome to explain: the current completed cell/status.json evaluations show both parallel and serial passed all 120 of 120 tests. The concrete task-solving difference is that the parallel-mode run entered swarm mode but did not execute child-agent delegation, instead using one main agent plus a background shell scan, while the serial run remained a single main-agent implementation with a somewhat different module split and broader local differential test. These differences did not produce a quality difference.
parallel_contributors: Swarm mode was enabled, but the main agent intentionally kept the task local and used only a background shell scan for currency discovery.
serial_contributors: The serial main agent also handled probing, implementation, integration, and verification locally and passed the same official evaluator.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used decimal.mjs while serial used pydecimal.mjs and an extra pystr.mjs helper; both artifact sets satisfied the evaluator.
Serial local differential testing reported expected help-program-name mismatches, while parallel normalized that path in a separate check; neither became an official failure.
